title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation), written in the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower period. In the surrounding pages he studies pairs (ρ,σ) of 2×2 matrices, viewed projectively as images of generators of π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) in a PGL_2-type group (written ΓPG on the next page).

The normalisations from the previous page are:
- ε_0 = −σ^{-1}ρ and ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1} are unipotent;
- Tr(ρ+σ) = 1 (u_1 = 1) and det ρ = det σ = v.

The modular case is det = 1 with Tr ρ = 1 and Tr σ = 0. There ρ and σ are projectively of order 3 and 2, ε_1 = (1 0; 1 1) and ε_0 = (1 −1; 0 1), so the pair generates PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. The general family deforms this modular representation.

Part 1 of the page: choice of pinning. A 'pinning' (épinglage) is a choice among four natural normalisations. These come from the pair of cyclic subgroups {L_0, L_1} (the inertia subgroups at 0 and 1) and the four generators ε_0^{±1}, ε_1^{±1}. Grothendieck explains why he normalises with L_1, putting ε_1 = (1 0; 1 1):
- this gives the most convenient form of the loop equation;
- historically he had first insisted on privileging L_0 (§44), and the definitive notation only appears in §45;
- choosing ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1} rather than its inverse −σρ^{-1} reflects preferring ρ over σ = σ_∞. The loop equation is written [α,ρ] = [β,σ]ε_1(ν) rather than [β,σ] = [α,ρ]ε_1^{-1}(ν).
- Swapping ρ and σ turns ε_1 into ε_1^{-1}.

Part 2 of the page: triples. The triple (l̃'_∞, l̃'_1, l̃'_0) = (ρ̃^{-1}, σ̃, ε̃_0) has product 1, so ε̃_0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃. The group S_3' (cf. §42 I) acts on such triples in two ways:
- by cyclic permutations;
- by inverting all three entries and reversing their order, giving (ε̃_0^{-1}, σ̃^{-1}, ρ̃), which a cyclic permutation turns into (σ̃^{-1}, ρ̃, ε̃_0^{-1}).

The next page identifies this last operation with the swap (ρ,σ) ↦ (σ,ρ), i.e. with the automorphism τ'_∞ of π_{0,3}. The inversion (ρ,σ) ↦ (ρ^{-1},σ^{-1}) becomes τ_∞. Together they generate a Klein four-group inside Aut_ext(π_{0,3}) that stabilises L_0.

Purpose. This is bookkeeping: it fixes a normalisation convention and tracks how the obvious symmetries of the representation variety act on it.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Check 1: ρ^{-1}σ(σ^{-1}ρ) = 1. Check 2: ε_0^{-1}σ^{-1}ρ = ρ^{-1}σσ^{-1}ρ = 1. Check 3: σ^{-1}ρε_0^{-1} = 1. Check 4: under ρ↔σ, −ρσ^{-1} becomes −σρ^{-1} = ε_1^{-1}.
Minor point: the signs in ε_i = −(…) are dropped silently when passing to the projective (tilde) elements. This is harmless in PGL_2.

ideas.what: Normalisation (pinning) of a 2-dimensional projective representation of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with unipotent local monodromies, so that one unipotent generator becomes (1 0; 1 1), deforming the modular representation onto PSL_2(Z)
ideas.modern_name: normal forms for SL_2/PGL_2 character varieties of the thrice-punctured sphere; parabolic (unipotent) monodromy normalisation

ideas.what: Action of the extended outer automorphism group of π_{0,3} (S_3 together with orientation reversal) on triples (l_∞', l_1', l_0') with product 1; the Klein four-subgroup generated by τ_∞, τ'_∞ stabilising L_0 realises the swap and the inversion of (ρ,σ)
ideas.modern_name: action of Out^*(F_2) ≅ S_3×Z/2 on the boundary data of the trinion / P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; used in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Aut_ext of the fundamental groupoids of M_{0,n} in general terms

ideas.what: Autobiographical note: in §44 he first privileged L_0 in the loop equation, and the definitive notation [α,ρ] = [β,σ]ε_1(ν) only appears in §45
ideas.modern_name: history of the 'équation des lacets' manuscript

missed.claim: Internal history of the loop-equation notes: the definitive normalisation (privileging L_1 and ρ, with ε_1 = (1 0; 1 1)) came after 'laborious wanderings' that privileged L_0 in §44. This is useful for anyone editing the 'équation des lacets' corpus, but it is not a new mathematical result.
missed.quote: à laquelle j'ai fini par parvenir d'ailleurs après des pérégrinations assez laborieuses, où c'est L_0 que je m'obstinais à privilégier dans les formules - cf §44, la notation définitive n'apparaît qu'au §45
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It helps reconstruct the chronology and conventions of Grothendieck's unpublished loop equation, the analogue of Drinfeld's GT relations, when reading §§44–45.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is notational bookkeeping: which of four pinnings to use, and how the obvious S_3/Klein-four symmetries act on triples with product 1. The mathematics is elementary and correct. The only distinctive content is the remark on how his notation evolved between §44 and §45.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '[?]-groupes' is very likely 'sous-groupes' (the pair of subgroups {L_0, L_1}).
'une paire unité' is doubtful in the hand; it may be 'une paire ordonnée' or similar. Uncertain.
Line 2: 'de l'un [-et de-] l'autre' should read 'de l'un et de l'autre', with a struck-out word before the inserted 'et de'.
'et par changement [?] en (ε̃_0^{-1}, σ̃^{-1}, …)': the word is uncertain in the image. Mathematically it denotes inversion together with reversal of order.
'quitte à se ramener' is plausible; the hand looks like 'quitte à se ramener ensuite par permutation circulaire'.
